text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates. One key habit is following naming conventions: choose clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another important practice is writing small, focused functions that each do one job well. This makes your code simpler and easier to test. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because when problems appear, you can find and fix them quickly. In short, writing clean code saves time and reduces mistakes in the long run.
